column171: Nurse-Midwife - Renal Unit | Motebang Hospital Lesotho | September 2021 – Present Provide comprehensive nursing care to patients with acute and chronic kidney disease. Perform and monitor hemodialysis treatments in accordance with prescribed dialysis regimens. Assess vascular access (AV Fistula, grafts, and central venous catheters) before, during, and after dialysis. Initiate, monitor, and terminate dialysis sessions safely. Closely monitor patients for complications such as hypotension, cramps, and access infections. Administer prescribed medications including anticoagulants, erythropoietin, IV iron, and antihypertensive. Maintain strict infection prevention and control measures within the dialysis unit. Monitor fluid balance, electrolyte levels, and laboratory results. Supervise and mentor junior nurses and supporting staff. Participate in multidisciplinary ward rounds with nephrologists and dieticians. Participate in audits and quality improvement initiatives within the renal unit. Educate patients and families on fluid restriction, renal diet, medication adherence, and vascular access care. Nurse-Midwife - Covid-19 Frontline | Motebang Hospital Lesotho | February 2020 – June 2020 Collected nasopharyngeal swabs for Covid-19 testing. Provided direct nursing care to confirmed and suspected Covid-19 patients. Monitored for respiratory distress and early signs of clinical deterioration. Provided emotional support to isolated patients and communicated updates to families, reassuring those directly affected. Conducted contact tracing in families in remote places for those confirmed positive. Provided health education on Covid-19 and proper precautions to follow to prevent and control it. Maintained accurate documentation and participated in multidisciplinary care planning. Nurse-Midwife - Maternity Ward | Motebang Hospital Lesotho | December 2019 – February 2020 Conducted comprehensive antenatal assessments (history taking, physical examination). Screened for high-risk conditions including pre-eclampsia, gestational diabetes, and anemia. Performed abdominal palpations to determine fetal positions. Conducted deliveries and monitored labour progress, including partograph interpretation. Performed immediate newborn assessment and basic neonatal resuscitation. Administered prescribed medications including oxytocin and magnesium sulphate. Promoted breastfeeding and provided postnatal education and family planning counseling. Collaborated with multidisciplinary teams to ensure safe maternal and neonatal outcomes. Maintained infection prevention and control standards and accurate clinical documentation. KEY COMPETENCIES & EXPERTISE Clinical Nursing & Midwifery: Kidney Failure Hemodialysis, Dialysis care and Renal patient management, Midwifery and labour management, Conducting deliveries in labour ward, Antenatal, intrapartum, and postnatal care, Neonatal assessment and immediate newborn care. General Nursing Care: Patient nursing management in general and surgical wards, Patient-Centered and Holistic Nursing care, Maternal and child health care. Public Health & Safety: Infection prevention and control, Patient Counseling and Health Education. Administration & Leadership: Supervisory and management skills, Data collection and Medical documentation, Multidisciplinary team collaboration.

column171: This candidate is a highly experienced Registered Nurse with 8 years of experience, specializing in Medical ICU and Infection Prevention and Control. Working at Life Springs Parkland Hospital (247 Beds), the candidate has extensive critical care experience in a Medical ICU (14 beds, NPR 1:1/1:2). The candidate demonstrates strong familiarity with a wide range of critical cases, including acute asthma, stroke, renal failure, and diabetes/DKA, and is proficient in operating advanced ICU equipment such as ventilators, cardiac monitors, and dialysis machines. The candidate's responsibilities include comprehensive patient assessments, advanced life support, medication administration, and strict adherence to infection prevention and control practices. Employer: Life Springs Parkland Hospital (247 Beds) Employment date: 2018 - Present Role: Registered Nurse Unit: Medical ICU (14 beds, NPR 1:1/1:2) Responsibilities: Conducts comprehensive assessments of critically ill patients, monitors vital signs, neurological status, and overall condition continuously. Provides advanced life support, including managing mechanical ventilators, administering oxygen therapy, and monitoring non-invasive ventilation such as CPAP and BiPAP. Administers prescribed medications, inotropes, sedatives, and IV fluids, ensuring accurate dosage, infusion rates, and monitoring for adverse reactions. Manages invasive lines such as arterial lines, central venous pressure (CVP) lines, and urinary catheters, maintaining sterility and proper functioning. Performs suctioning, wound care, dressing changes, and care for drains such as chest tubes, or VAC systems. Assists with diagnostic and therapeutic procedures, including ECG monitoring, ABG sampling, and preparing patients for imaging or surgeries. Monitors and operates advanced ICU equipment such as ventilators, infusion pumps, cardiac monitors, defibrillators, and dialysis machines. Implements individualized care plans based on patient needs, collaborating with the multidisciplinary team to optimize outcomes. Provides emotional support and clear communication to patients’ families regarding condition updates, prognosis, and care plans. Participates in emergencies such as cardiac arrests, code blues, sepsis management, and rapid response situations, following ACLS and ICU protocols. Ensures strict infection prevention and control practices, maintains aseptic techniques, and adheres to hospital and ICU policies. Maintains accurate and detailed documentation of patient care, progress, and any changes in condition for continuity of care. Assists in end-of-life care and advanced directives discussions with compassion and professionalism. Educates patients and families about post-ICU recovery, rehabilitation needs, and follow-up care where applicable. Participates in staff mentoring, orientation, and continuous professional development to maintain high standards of critical care nursing. Ensures ICU equipment, emergency trolleys, and supplies are checked, stocked, and ready for use at all times. Collaborates with physicians, respiratory therapists, physiotherapists, dietitians, and other specialists to provide holistic care. Supports quality improvement initiatives, audits, and research projects to enhance ICU nursing practice and patient outcomes. Manages pain and sedation effectively, using validated scales to monitor patient comfort and adjust care accordingly. Provides psychosocial support to families coping with critical illness or bereavement, respecting cultural and ethical considerations. Types of Cases Managed: Acute asthma, COPD, seizures, stroke, renal failure, gastro-enteritis, overdose, diabetes/DKA, uncontrolled hypertension, respiratory failure, pneumonia Equipment Used: Cardiac monitor with sats probe, BP cuff and ECG leads, temp probe, Baxter machine, drip stand, suction, foot pumps, air mattress, ventilator, high flow, bear hugger, ECG machine, nasal cannula, face mask, emergency trolley, defibrillator, drug cupboard, central line, A-line, beds, negative pressure isolation room for TB/Covid, gloves, apron, bed table, bed locker, red bins, general waste bin, sluice, bedpans/urinary.

column171: Florence Khumalo is a highly dedicated Registered Nurse with over two years of specialized experience in the Operating Theatre, supplemented by an initial role in a High Care unit. She is proficient in both scrub and circulating roles, managing a broad range of cases across surgical specialties including ENT, Orthopaedics (e.g., total knee/hip replacement, ORIF), Plastics (e.g., breast augmentation, abdominoplasty), Urology, and General Surgery. Her technical competence is demonstrated by her familiarity with advanced equipment such as the ROSA knee replacement machine, Diathermy, various surgical camera stacks (urology, orthopaedics, gynaecology, ENT), and the CoolSeal machine. Ensured safe handling, labeling, and transfer of surgical specimens according to policy. Participated in post-operative debriefing, cleaning, restocking, and preparation of the theatre for subsequent cases. column171: Professional nurse currently working in the maternity unit:Post Natal unit planning care for post NVD and C section mothers and babies in the nursery. Bed capacity is 30 and average occupancy 90-100% and NPR1:30. Skilled in managing post delivery mothers and monitoring babies from birth to discharge. Performs assessment of head to toe for newborns and observations done for mothers for bleeding, PPH, wound care management, observation for pad checks to assess blood loss post delivery, pain management, athether care, antibiotic management and assisting mother with all her activities for the first 24 hours post section. Establishes breast feeding, involved in education especially for first time mothers on feeding, bathing, chord care. Works in collaboration with the tam ensuring that rooming in of the baby is practiced. Involve the family in the care process from admission to discharge Employer: Chris Hani Baragwanath Employment date: 09/2024 - Present Role: Registered Nurse Unit: Postnatal Ward NPR 1:30 Responsibilities: Monitoring and supporting newborn feeding, ensuring the baby is latching correctly during breastfeeding or taking adequate formula if bottle-fed. Assessing the newborn regularly for signs of jaundice and escalating care if required. Monitoring newborn vital signs including temperature, heart rate, respiratory rate, and oxygen saturation at prescribed intervals. Administering routine newborn immunisations as per hospital protocol and national immunisation schedule. Caring for neonates under phototherapy by positioning the baby correctly, monitoring serum bilirubin (SBR) levels, ensuring eye protection is used, and maintaining fluid balance. Providing post-operative nursing care to mothers who have undergone caesarean sections, including wound monitoring, pain management, and mobility assistance. Administering analgesia and other prescribed medications via oral, intravenous, or intramuscular routes, while monitoring for side effects and effectiveness. Delivering postnatal health education to mothers, covering topics such as wound care, breastfeeding techniques, infant bathing, postnatal exercises, contraception, and signs of complications. Monitoring postpartum bleeding to detect early signs of haemorrhage and reporting abnormalities promptly. Monitoring maternal vital signs and general condition following delivery to ensure early identification of complications such as infection, hypertension, or thromboembolism. Encouraging and supporting mothers in initiating and maintaining effective infant feeding, offering guidance for both breastfeeding and formula feeding. Documenting all assessments, interventions, medication administrations, and patient education activities accurately and in a timely manner. Supervising junior nurses, enrolled nurses, and support staff to ensure care delivery is aligned with clinical standards and ward routines. Assisting doctors with bedside procedures such as wound dressing, catheter insertion, removal of sutures, and postnatal examinations. Ensuring infection prevention measures are followed in both maternal and newborn care, including hand hygiene, proper handling of breast pumps, and umbilical cord care. Coordinating discharge planning by ensuring mothers and babies are medically fit, providing discharge education, and arranging follow-up appointments. Providing emotional support and reassurance to new mothers, especially those experiencing anxiety, baby blues, or difficulty adjusting to parenthood. Participating in ward handovers, team meetings, and clinical audits to maintain continuity of care and support quality improvement initiatives. Maintaining proper stock levels of medications, consumables, and newborn supplies, and reporting any shortages or equipment issues to management. Responding appropriately to maternal or neonatal emergencies, initiating emergency protocols, and collaborating with the multidisciplinary team for timely intervention.
column259: Employer: King Fahad Medical City Employment date: 07/2022 - 07/2023 Role: Registered Nurse Unit: Labour Ward Responsibilities: Preparing all essential medical equipment before patient admission including the cardiotocography (CTG) machine, resuscitative equipment, oxygen, suction units, and ensuring all equipment in the assigned delivery room is clean, functional, and ready for use. Receiving a detailed handover from the previous primary nurse using the ISBAR communication framework to ensure continuity of care and patient safety. Reviewing and verifying all antenatal records on patient admission such as laboratory results, antenatal profiles, ultrasound reports, and medical or obstetric history. Assuming full accountability for assessing, planning, implementing, and evaluating comprehensive nursing care throughout the antepartum, intrapartum, and immediate postpartum periods. Monitoring maternal vital signs and fetal heart rate continuously or intermittently as indicated to assess labour progression and detect early signs of complications. Recognizing and responding promptly to any changes in the patient’s condition and reporting concerns immediately to the attending physician and the shift in charge. Providing structured health education to women during labour on breathing techniques, pain relief options, birthing positions, and what to expect during each stage of labour. Educating and supporting new mothers after birth on personal hygiene, perineal care, breastfeeding techniques, and the importance of early mother-infant bonding. Offering emotional support and compassionate care to mothers experiencing difficult outcomes such as miscarriage, stillbirth, or neonatal death, and referring them for additional psychosocial support if needed. Preparing the delivery room by adhering to strict infection prevention and control protocols, using appropriate personal protective equipment, and ensuring a sterile environment for childbirth. Performing normal vaginal deliveries independently for low-risk pregnancies and managing immediate post-delivery care, including performing episiotomy repair and suturing first- and second-degree perineal tears. Providing immediate care to the newborn including drying, APGAR scoring, initiating skin-to-skin contact, and supporting early initiation of breastfeeding. Assisting mothers with positioning and latching during breastfeeding and closely observing for any signs of postpartum complications such as excessive bleeding or retained placenta. Conducting wellness screenings for pregnant women including measurement of body mass index (BMI), blood pressure, random or fasting blood glucose, and cholesterol levels as part of routine antenatal assessments. Assisting doctors or midwives with complex deliveries, caesarean section preparation, and emergency obstetric procedures when required. Documenting all patient care activities, observations, medications, and interventions accurately and promptly in maternity records and labour charts. Participating in multidisciplinary rounds, ward meetings, and clinical audits to improve care quality and ensure patient safety standards are upheld. Supervising student nurses and newly appointed staff during clinical procedures, reinforcing evidence-based practices and maternity protocols.

column171: Employer: Mediclinic Legae Hospital (142 Beds) Employment date: 08/2023 - Present Role: Registered Nurse Unit: Maternity Ward (28 Beds, NPR 1:6) Responsibilities: Provide holistic nursing care to antenatal, intrapartum, and postnatal women. Perform routine maternal assessments including vital signs, abdominal palpation, fetal heart rate monitoring, and obstetric examinations. Administer prescribed medications, IV fluids, and pain management interventions safely. Monitor labour progression using partographs and respond promptly to deviations from normal. Assist with and conduct normal vaginal deliveries while ensuring safe maternal and neonatal outcomes. Support obstetricians during assisted deliveries and emergency procedures such as caesarean sections. Provide immediate newborn care including neonatal resuscitation if required. Perform APGAR scoring and continuous monitoring of the newborn’s condition. Educate mothers on breastfeeding, newborn hygiene, bonding, and routine postnatal care. Perform wound care including post-surgical dressing changes and episiotomy care. Manage postpartum complications such as hemorrhage, infection, and thromboembolism risk. Conduct family planning education and provide contraceptive counselling. Ensure safe infection prevention and control practices at all times. Maintain accurate documentation of assessments, care interventions, and clinical outcomes. Coordinate care with multidisciplinary teams such as doctors, midwives, paediatricians, and social workers. Ensure safe transfer or referral of high-risk mothers and infants to higher level facilities when required. Provide emotional, psychological, and compassionate support to mothers, newborns, and families. Monitor and manage obstetric emergencies such as preeclampsia, eclampsia, fetal distress, or cord prolapse. Administer and monitor vaccinations for newborns according to immunisation schedules. Perform health education focused on lifestyle management, antenatal follow-up, and postpartum recovery. Support and guide junior staff, students, and enrolled nurses in delivering quality maternity care. Ensure availability and proper functioning of maternity equipment and emergency supplies. Participate in quality assurance activities, audits, and maternal-neonatal safety initiatives. Promote a safe and respectful birthing environment that upholds patient dignity and informed decision-making. Types of Cases Managed: Antenatal patients with routine or high-risk pregnancies, women in labour, post normal vaginal delivery patients, post-caesarean patients, post-gynaecological procedure patients, and newborn babies. Equipment Used: Fetal heart rate monitors (CTG machines), maternal vital signs monitors, stethoscope, blood pressure machine, pulse oximeter, thermometer, delivery beds, obstetric forceps, vacuum extractors, episiotomy scissors, suturing kits, infusion pumps and IV stands, oxygen cylinders and masks, suction machines, neonatal resuscitation equipment, infant warmers, incubators, and phototherapy units.

column259: Employer: Alberton Netcare Hospital Employment date: 02/2018 - 07/2024 Role: Registered Nurse Unit: NNICU Responsibilities: Assess, monitor, and document the vital signs and overall condition of critically ill and premature neonates. Coordinate with allied health professionals such as respiratory therapists, dietitians, and physiotherapists to ensure comprehensive neonatal care.

Provide post-operative and post-procedural care for high-risk surgical and medical patients. Implement and maintain infection prevention and control measures using aseptic and isolation techniques. Ensure pressure injury prevention, wound care, and skin integrity management for critically ill patients. Maintain accurate, detailed, and legally compliant nursing documentation and clinical records. Collaborate closely with intensivists, doctors, physiotherapists, pharmacists, and the multidisciplinary team to deliver coordinated care. Provide emotional support, education, and clear communication to patients and their families in the ICU setting. Ensure safe operation, monitoring, and troubleshooting of ICU equipment including ventilators, infusion pumps, monitors, and dialysis machines. Participate in structured handovers, ward rounds, audits, and quality improvement initiatives. Support end-of-life care, ethical decision-making, and palliative management when required. Supervise, mentor, and support junior nursing staff, student nurses, and support personnel. Adhere strictly to hospital policies, professional standards, ethical guidelines, and legal requirements related to critical care nursing. Equipment Used: Baxter machines, ventilators such as Hamilton, Vela, and Dräger, cardiac monitors, Kangaroo pumps, blood pressure cuffs, ECG machine, emergency trolley.
